originality.rationale: The 2022 primary full text establishes only the distance-hereditary/non-real-stability classification, not the simultaneous strict pairwise covariance signs or exact wheel adjacent current-square certificate. The 2023 weighted stability theorem is likewise not a covariance theorem. Transfer-current covariance is known generally but its off-diagonal vertex-degree sign for adjacent wheel vertices does not follow immediately because a shared edge contributes a positive term. The explicit polynomial square certificate resolves this obstruction, and comparison with the positive covariance of the bare cycle makes it a motivated separation. Residual risks remain from implicit classical applications and inaccessible wheel-subtree literature.

value.rationale: Real stability is a powerful global negative-dependence criterion, while pairwise degree repulsion at unit weights is a natural weaker diagnostic. Wheels form a simple infinite family with the criterion failing but all degrees still negatively correlated. The sign of adjacent rim degree covariance is non-obvious due to the single shared edge, and its exact completed-square identity resolves this substantive competition; the bare-cycle positive-sign comparison shows a genuine structural change.
